patches.title: Moving on Up: 42.22 Pre-Release
patches.content: Hello again, Survivors! We have news on the upcoming 42.22 Update, available for testing now on our new Pre-Release branch, which replaces the Unstable branch for early testing. Yes, we changed the branch name, as it was causing some confusion among players, especially given the (long) history of Unstable in Build 42. What does this mean to you? For the average player, absolutely nothing. We recommend you keep on enjoying Project Zomboid on the default Stable branch, currently 42.21, while pre-release goes through final vetting. If, however, you are a modder, a multiplayer server admin or just the brave, testing-friendly type who is willing to test and break things before they go live to the broader public, then you can opt-in to the Pre-Release. How to update Project Zomboid to access Pre-Release 1. Back up any Project Zomboid save games you want to come back to, just in case. 2. Right-click Project Zomboid in your Steam Library. 3. Select “Properties”. 4. Under “Game Versions & Betas” select “Pre-Release” Going forward, we’ll be releasing builds into the Pre-Release branch before they go forward to the Stable branch (barring urgent hotfixes that may need to go directly to Stable). The goal here is to identify any issues that need to be addressed, while also allowing server admins and modders a chance to look under the hood for upcoming changes. We plan on keeping a build in the Pre-Release branch for at least one week before it moves to the Stable branch. We really want to stress though; don’t move your long-term singleplayer save over to the Pre-Release branch unless you have backed up that save! We cannot guarantee that the save will work and/or you will be able to use it in the final release, which will come after Pre-Release testing is complete. In summary, the cycle for a new update is: New update released -> deployed to Pre-Release branch -> Tested, one week minimum -> deployed to Stable branch. If, during Pre-Release testing, bugs are discovered that would benefit from another revision of the update, we’ll do that, and keep you in the loop if it happens via our community channels (our forums, Reddit and Discord primarily). patches.title: A Note on Java Mods and Modding
patches.content: The modding community for Project Zomboid is huge and incredibly diverse, ranging from tiny system changes to massive overhauls. We're endlessly grateful to modders who spend their time making and maintaining mods, whether they're big or small. Recently we've seen an explosion in creativity and potential with mods, with some completely changing the way Project Zomboid is played - a whole new perspective, you might say. This is possible thanks to mods being written in Java, which is the core coding language of Project Zomboid. With the help of Java-based loaders and frameworks, modders can create mods that change the game at a fundamental level and let their imaginations run free. That creativity is exciting, but it is important to understand the risks involved, both for your game and potentially your computer. Download Mods Responsibly As with any third-party software, you should only download and run mods from sources and authors you trust. This applies to all mods, regardless of the coding language they are written in. In the vast majority of cases Java mods require manual installation, ask you to download files from external websites, require a special loader, or generally instruct you to do things beyond simply clicking ‘Subscribe’ on the Steam Workshop. They are, as described, written in Java, the same coding language as Project Zomboid. As such, they are able to change the game’s code directly. This is what allows them to change the game in radical ways, but also means that they can, potentially, be used to create security vulnerabilities. Unlike regular Lua mods, Java mods are outside the “confines” of Project Zomboid’s code. If a Lua mod repaints your house and adds new wallpaper, a Java mod builds a new house nearby - which could even be built without you knowing, and then have an additional, unseen back door. This does not mean all Java mods are inherently malicious, or that installing one will automatically put your computer at risk. However, it does mean that Java mods require a different level of trust. You are not simply installing new game content; you are allowing third-party code to run on your machine. We strongly encourage you to look for mods...

patches.title: Build 42.21 Stable Released
patches.content: We released 42.21 into our Unstable beta last Wednesday, and extend our thanks to the community for checking it over and kicking the tires! If you’ve just seen your game updating and want to know what’s new, then read on below. Full patchnotes however can be found here. Going forward, this should be the standard procedure for all releases; a new update goes to Unstable, it’s tested by you, we potentially make more changes, and ultimately the release goes to Stable. In this instance the community did not report any major issues, so the ‘Go’ button is being pressed… today. Main Stuff • We have tackled the worst offending bugs when it came to issues of zombie duplication in MP, and issues in which zombies would disappear after a player left and re-entered a “chunk” of the game world in both SP and MP. These issues were particularly obvious in larger zombie population games and as such impacted a lot of our hardcore players. You should find your game much improved on this count, although there are still some instances of this which we have on our radar and will be fixed in our next update. • A common piece of feedback since the launch of B42 Stable has been the new ‘XXL trees’ occasionally getting in the way of the player - especially when driving. 42.21 contains changes to the XXL tree cutaway behaviour: they now cutaway better for players in vehicles, they no longer hide houses and furniture they overhang, and their overall transparency has been adjusted for better overall visibility. The work in 42.21 will make your life easier, but is a work in progress and will receive more love in future. • In 42.20.4 the “loadstring” and “loadstream” lua methods were disabled to help address security vulnerabilities. After investigating further into the security issue, we’ve decided to re-enable those commands. Sorry for the disruption, modders/server admins! Plus, clearly, much more. As mentioned, the full changelist can be found here on the Indie Stone forums. Big Thanks While we have your attention we also wanted to extend our thanks to Scribl (Boris) and Rasmus Moorats (nnsee) for their aid in flagging security vulnerabilities that were fixed in 42.20.4. patches.title: Re-population of the Dead: Build 42.21 Unstable Released
patches.content: {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/3ab5ae515b648cc78730233a9d4d103ccae889a8.png Hello Survivors! We’re back, and we have a new update, which is now available to play and test on the Unstable branch on Steam. As our first incremental update post-Build 42, this update contains fixes and updates for a whole bunch of things, and we’d love your feedback on them. How to update your Project Zomboid game client to access Unstable 1. Right-click Project Zomboid in your Steam Library. 2. Select “Properties”. 3. Under “Game Versions & Betas” select “Unstable”. {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4460946/f6e3f5b10e52b75e8fb54e02536be214f579cc74.jpg Existing savegames on Build 42.20.4 should not be affected by this update, however, if you want to test 42.21 with an existing save, we highly recommend manually backing up your save before attempting to play it on the Unstable branch. If you do discover issues with an existing savegame, please let us know via the forums. What’s in this update? 42.21 is an incremental update and has a lot of fixes, but also a few gameplay improvements. These are relatively minor, but hopefully will improve your “quality of survival” in your personal zombie apocalypse. Below are some highlights; for a complete set of changes and fixes, check out the full update notes on our forums. Big Ticket Items Fix: As many will know, we had an issue in which zombies would disappear after a player left and re-entered a “chunk” of the game world; this was particularly obvious in larger zombie population games and as such impacted a lot of our hardcore players. This has now been fixed in both SP and MP. It was a tricky fix for us to pin down and remedy at its root, but is now ready to face the hordes via the Unstable branch. Fix: Issues of zombie duplication in MP have also been tackled, and we’d ask you to be on the look out for any other instances you spot once Unstable is live. Updated: A common piece of feedback since the launch of B42 Stable has been the new ‘XXL trees’ occasionally getting in the way of the player – especially when driving. 42.21 contains changes to the XXL tree cutaway behaviour: they now cutaway better for players in vehicles, they no longer hide houses and furn...

patches.title: 42.20.4 STABLE & 42.19.2 UNSTABLE & 41.78.21 LEGACY Hotfixes Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. FIXES Fixed security vulnerabilities. Mod makers should be aware that as part of this fix, the loadstring and loadstream methods have been removed. If your mods used these methods you will need to update your mods. If you were using these methods to execute code sent from the server, then you will need to create the necessary methods and call them by sending the appropriate commands. If you are unable to replace these methods in your case, please report the issue in the #mod_portal channel of The Official Project Zomboid Discord server, explaining how you were using them As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.3 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. MP Improved server player limit handling, including support for up to 254 players and administrator access when servers are full Fixed an issue that would cause the client to hang on "Loading Map" forever FIXES Addressed multiple causes of a memory leak that could lead to performance degradation and crashes over time If you continue to encounter an out of memory error in a new save, please submit a bug report with your logs and profiler video from debug so the team can investigate Implemented several memory optimisations Reduced instances of black and gray boxes appearing when travelling quickly through the world Additional causes of this issue are still being investigated and will be addressed in a future update Fixed issues that could cause errors during lighting updates. As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.2 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. TECHNICAL/DEBUG Fixed percent symbol handling in files Mods should use %% to display % characters A temporary workaround was implemented to allow both methods of processing, however mod makers should update their mods to use %% to display % characters going forward as this workaround will be removed in a future unstable update Error logs will be populated highlighting the error so mod makers can see what needs to be updated going forward Fixed quick tips displaying % as %% Added memory debug-information when showing fps debug info As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.

patches.title: 42.20.1 STABLE Hotfix Released
patches.content: While this update should not break saves, if you encounter any bugs please ensure you can replicate them on a fresh save with no mods installed before reporting them to our team here. MP Improved Lua checksum validation for multiplayer anti-cheat Fixed an issue that caused significant performance problems with chunk unloading on multiplayer servers This should fix most of the bugs players were getting on high-pop servers due to server lag Fixed errors and crashes that could occur when selecting Multiplayer while certain languages were selected Fixed an issue where vehicles could temporarily disappear for players after another player disconnected Fixed an issue that would allow broken B41 worlds to be hosted on B42 servers Fixed an issue where players switching from b41 to B42 could be met with a missing menu FIXES Improved memory usage by reusing discarded world data Fixed a memory leak that could lead to performance degradation and crashes over time If you continue to encounter an out of memory error in a new save, please submit a bug report with your logs and profiler video from debug so the team can investigate Fixed a rare exception that could occur during exploration TECHNICAL/DEBUG Added the ability for mods to write .json files Fixed percent symbol handling in translation files Mod translations should use %% to display % characters As always, discussions regarding this update can be found pinned to the Project Zomboid Discussions Forums here.
